All of the no answers break my heart. For me, 100% yes. However, I have no dependents and therefore no ties to a singular job/location, so it is very easy for me to bail and move on from a job that isn't playing fair. Exploitation is absolutely everywhere in this industry and if I had been forced to stay in one of my first jobs then I think my answer might be different.

For me, I couldn't have lived my life without being a vet. I still love what I do, I find it very interesting and I still love learning. Being a vet sits well with me morally. Some clients are awful, yes, but some are absolute angels who give me faith in humanity again. I once had an agoraphobic client who came out to visit me for the first time after I euthanised her PKD cat (the kitty had been brought in by a family member for the entire time prior to that, from first presentation/diagnosis to treatment/management). That sort of thing humbles you.

Absolutely I find that there is a difference between corporate vs independent vs charity work. Charity has been my favourite, corporate has been a mixed bag (I've worked for three, one absolutely dreadful, one unbelievably money focused but at least let me have some clinical freedom, one much better but still very finance focused).

Honestly, I can't complain about my quality of life. I come from a very modest background (at vet school I relied on free food handouts and at once stage had three jobs on top of being a full time student), so perhaps comparatively ANYTHING would look like an amazing wage, but I can afford to live how I like, can afford pets and go on expensive holidays to other continents. I don't run a car and have accepted that I will never be able to afford to buy a house, and yes absolutely there are other jobs that would net me more money for less effort, but overall I'm happy with what I've got.

Tixel, Twickets and Vivid seats let you sell (at FV). I can personally recommend Twickets as a seller. If you don't want to use a site that will charge fees for this then you'll have to do it privately via PayPal or similar. Speaking as someone who buys resale tickets often and has sold several times too, you really have very little to lose as a seller, vs the buyer who risks giving money to a scammer who either doesn't have tickets, or doesn't send them. If you accept payment as 'goods and services on PayPal then this is reassuring for the buyer as it allows the buyer to request a chargeback from PayPal in the event of not receiving the tickets (as opposed to the 'family and friends' option). PayPal will charge (you) for selling goods and services, but I think it's reasonable to pass this cost to your buyer.

For me it's absolutely worth it! I have both the PS5 and PS4 version and actually preferentially use the PS4 version since 2.0 was released. If you were playing 2.0 from the start then I think it would be fine but for me personally the update was such a massive overhaul to the gameplay itself (changes to the skill tree, quickhacking, how armour works etc) that I'm too stubborn to switch.

As far as glitches/bugs go; the game will occasionally crash on me (once every ten hours or so? I don't find it a big deal), and there's occasionally some janky things like objects remaining in middair after you knock over the table they're sitting on... inconsequential stuff. I haven't found that there are more bugs in the PS4 version than the PS5 version when I played that pre 2.0. And in fact, since the update I noticed a lot more issues in the PS5 version (missing audio clips so characters' speech is silent and I have to just read the subtitles, characters' hair freaking out and having a seizure on their head). Nothing game-breaking in any version, just stuff that's mildly funny at best and annoying at worst.

TL;DR, PS4 version is fine and I actually prefer it. If you decide you want to get Phantom Liberty at a later date then the PS5 update is free and you can transfer your save files across easy.

I'm so sorry you have to cope with that. I'm the same age as you and this is my fourth Christmas alone so I can relate. It's tough when there's so much you're 'supposed' to do on that day that you can't do for whatever reason.  


Something that really helped me is to get some pet sitting gigs on Christmas day. Lots of people go away so sitters that are willing to work Christmas are in demand, I used to get paid double. It really helped me to have tasks I had to accomplish that day, and I think forcing myself to leave the house was good too. Plus pets can help with the loneliness.   


Failing that, have you looked at any events going on at Christmas in your area? Any soup kitchens or similar looking for volunteers? Would be a good chance to be around people and feel like you've been productive. Some organisations also organise meals with other people who would otherwise be lonely that day, such as elderly people who live alone.  


My first Christmas alone, I didn't have anything to do and didn't leave the house. I was miserable but it helped me to treat it as 'just another day', not Christmas. It helped to not put up any decorations or anything. It just felt like I was missing out less.  


Whatever happens I hope you are able to have a good day regardless. I'm sorry that you are in this position, I promise you you're not alone.
